beats.say: When a phone is lost, the biggest loss is often family photos. Protecting them takes a few minutes.
If you have seen a notification like this, the photos from recent months have no copy.
But careful: a message saying your storage is full and photos will be deleted is a favourite scam.

messages.text: Your storage is full. Your photos will be deleted in 24 hours.

beats.say: Turn on backup in the phone's own settings, then restore one photo to check it works.

scenes.prompt: Set up a backup on your phone. Put the steps in order.

items.label: Turn on automatic backup in Settings
Connect to Wi-Fi and a charger, wait for the first backup
Check that the last backup date is today
Open one photo on another device to test the restore

scenes.explain: A backup only helps when it works, so check the date and restore one photo. Protect the cloud account with two-step verification too.

scenes.prompt: Find the signs of a scam in this message.

messages.text: All your photos will be deleted within 24 hours.
Upgrade your plan for just 1.99 AZN:

spots.label: Storage full
spots.explain: When storage is full, new backups stop, but old photos are not deleted at once. Check storage yourself in the phone's settings.

spots.label: Deadline
spots.explain: Fear and a deadline push you to pay without thinking.

spots.label: Small amount
spots.explain: A small amount lowers your guard. The real goal is your card details.

spots.label: Strange domain
spots.explain: This is not the cloud service's domain. Change your plan only in the phone's settings.

scenes.title: Where are your photos?
scenes.intro: There are a few notifications on your phone. For each one, choose the step that protects your photos.

body.text: Last backup: 143 days ago. Turn it on now?

actions.label: Turn on backup
actions.feedback: Correct. From now on, photos are copied automatically every night.

actions.label: Later
actions.feedback: If the phone is lost today, five months of photos go with it. Turn on backup now.

messages.text: Your storage is full. Your photos will be deleted in 24 hours. Upgrade your plan:

steps.say: In the morning, a message like this arrives.

actions.label: Open link
actions.feedback: The link does not go to the cloud service's site. Check storage only in the phone's settings.

actions.label: Report as spam
actions.feedback: Well done. This is a fake: a real service does not threaten to delete your photos in a day.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Correct. Check your storage yourself in the settings.

actions.label: Pay 1.99 AZN
actions.feedback: Your card details went to the fraudster. Call the bank on the number on the back of the card right away and block it.

actions.label: Close page
actions.feedback: Good thing you stopped. Check your storage plan only in the phone's settings.

steps.say: You found a free backup app in the store.

actions.label: Deny
actions.feedback: Correct, a photo backup needs no access to texts or contacts. The phone's own backup is enough.

actions.label: Allow
actions.feedback: With text message access, the app can read your bank codes. Delete an app like this right away.

steps.say: A month later, the phone is lost on the metro. You sign in on a new phone.

actions.label: Restore
actions.feedback: Well done. Because backup was on, the family photos are all there.

actions.label: Set up as a new phone
actions.feedback: Then the photos will not come to the new phone. Restore from the backup.

nodes.text: In the evening you lost your phone on the metro. What do you do first when you get home?

choices.label: I lock the phone from another device and check where it is
choices.feedback: Correct. Locking stops the finder from reaching your photos and accounts.

choices.label: I wait till morning, maybe someone will call
choices.feedback: On an unlocked phone your accounts are at risk. Lock it right away.

choices.label: I post my number and address on social media
choices.feedback: Personal details give fraudsters a new chance. Lock the phone first.

nodes.text: The phone was not found. The next day a text arrives: "Your phone was found, sign in to see it".

messages.text: Your phone was found. Sign in to your account to see where it is: cihaz-tap.example.info

choices.label: I open the link and sign in
choices.feedback: This trap hunts people who lost a phone. Your account password goes straight to the fraudster.

choices.label: I do not open it, I restore the new phone from backup
choices.feedback: Well done. The photos are safe in the backup, and a message like this cannot be trusted.

points: Turn on automatic backup on your phone.
Restore one photo to check it.
"Storage full"? Check settings, not the link.
